_meta.purpose: The material index — the resolved 'blend-results' a voxel renders, AND the draw vocabulary every built voxel is placed with (a Maker's templates fetch and place these). A material is NOT an element; it is what an aggregate element-composition (periodic_table.json) CLASSIFIES to from a voxel's perspective, or what a thing was made into. Index space is 0-255; 186 rows are defined: 178 as of 2026-10-20 (P4 'fill the slots', from the compound catalog, rocks.json and the Prism books) and the eight emissive glows in 248-255 (2026-10-21); the free ids inside each band and 220-247 are left for Aaron.
_meta.classify: A voxel's material = the classifier's pick over its ledger (flicker-worldstate::classify_material, P2 of the materials-unification plan, 2026-08-19). Primary key: the DOMINANT COMPOUND by mass resolves through `represents`; fallback: best-match of the element composition against `signature` (full signature present, most-specific wins, lower id breaks ties). Derived, never stored as truth — recompute after any ledger change.
_meta.represents: Compound NAMES (exact, from the merged compound catalog — same scheme as rocks.json modal keys) whose dominance classifies a container to THIS material. Resolved + uniqueness-gated at load: an unknown name or two materials claiming one compound refuses to load. Rows without `represents` are reachable only via the signature fallback (Bedrock/Basalt/Shale/Gravel = generic rock ground). Ice and Lava carry none ON PURPOSE: same compounds as Water/rock under different CONDITIONS (T/P) — the v2 conditions hook of the R7 registry decides those, never composition alone.
_meta.render_class: REQUIRED on every row except the id-0 Air placeholder (never drawn). The closed 4-way render axis (Aaron, ratified 2026-08-19, amending the 2026-08-18 3-way): 'blendable' = top-surface terrain, participates in voxel primary/secondary/blend transitions; 'hard_edge' = rocks/ores/minerals, renders as itself, NEVER blended (blend forced 0 at mesh build) — the visual signature is player-facing information; 'translucent' = gems/ice/water/oil, the alpha/refraction path; 'emissive' = glowing, colours restricted to the curated palettes.json emissive set. Orthogonal to `category` (geological identity, free-form) — never merge the two.
_meta.traits: hardness (Mohs-like 0-10, erosion resistance), brittleness (0 ductile..1 shatters → sediment), water_capacity (0..1 porosity / how much water it holds), viscosity (0 flows freely each pass .. 1 static solid; governs how a flow-effect material moves per pass — water lowest, oil/lava mid, ice creeps high), density_g_cm3 (differentiation / weight). Authoritative here; element traits are the blend fallback. PROPOSED STARTING VALUES — tune.
_meta.render: color [r,g,b] 0-1 is a PLACEHOLDER palette (proposed starting values, tune by eye): the P1 palette-buffer wiring draws these on voxels until MaterialBench-defined bundles land per slot in package/materials/<id:03>/. The Material Catalog scene shows the whole byte.
_meta.effects_note: water / ice / lava are not stacked layers — they are tracked effects (persistent saturation/flow state) whose per-pass motion rate comes from viscosity. Water and Lava KEEP their material slots (Aaron, ruled 2026-08-19): the classifier needs an answer for a mostly-water/molten container; the fancy liquid rendering is a shader pass keyed off the slot, not a replacement for it.

bands.40-59: 40-59 ORES (every harvestable ore of the compound catalog)
bands.180-199: 180-199 BIOME SURFACES (the nine biomes of Book VII Appendix E)
bands.200-219: 200-219 PRISM LORE (Book IV reagents, Book VII)
bands._comment_248-255: EMISSIVE GLOWS: the eight curated glows, one per palettes.json emissive colour in palette order (see _meta.emissive_slots). The band LABEL stays a short noun phrase like its neighbours' - the Material Inspector shows it in one footer cell - and this note carries the explanation; the label's wording is Aaron's to tune. The eight glow rows are PLACEHOLDERS the agent authored on the curated palette (2026-10-21): their names ('Glow <colour>'), colours, traits and the look of their staged bundles (glow_materials.json) are Aaron's to tune.
bands._note: Authoring bands, not a loader gate — save the emissive slots 248-255, whose render class the loader gates (flicker_materials::slot_accepts: emissive rows only): the band says what KIND of material an id is for, so a new row lands beside its kin and the catalog reads in rows. Existing ids (10-14, 20-24, 40-43, 60-63) kept their slots; nothing was renumbered.

_meta.emissive_slots: 248-255: the EMISSIVE slots — reserved FOR emissive-class materials, not blocked (Aaron, 2026-10-20: 'reserve slots for emissive materials … those would be the emissive slots, not blocked out'). Eight slots, eight curated palettes.json colours. OPEN since 2026-10-21: flicker_materials::slot_accepts admits ONLY render_class 'emissive' here — the loader refuses any other class in these slots by name, and the MaterialBench commit and the PackageBench promotion ask the same predicate — while an emissive material stays legal anywhere else (Lava, 62). Filled with the eight glows Glow Red .. Glow Violet in palette order: PLACEHOLDERS, Aaron's to tune.
_meta.sources: Rows 2026-10-20: rocks.json (every rock, 10-39), compounds.json + crust_compounds.json (every harvestable ore 40-59, the minerals 70-83, the gemstones 90-99, the alloys drawn as families 100-119; `represents` claims resolve and are unique at load), Book III's plant system (woods/plants are species placeholders), Book VII Appendix E's nine biomes (180-192), Book IV's reagents by colour (200-206, their world-occurring forms). Rows 2026-10-21: the eight emissive glows 248-255 from palettes.json's curated set, in palette order. Trait values are proposed from real-world Mohs/density where known.
